content: The Global Malaria Programme of the World Health Organization (WHO) in Geneva, Switzerland, is led by Dr. Raman Velayudhan from the Department of Control of Neglected Tropical Diseases. The programme collaborates with various experts and organizations to develop guidelines and recommendations for malaria prevention and control. Members of the External Review Group (ERG) for 2021 and 2022 included Dr. Jenifer Armistead from the Malaria Division of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), Professor Maureen Coetzee from the University of the Witwatersrand in South Africa, Professor Umberto d’Alessandro, Director of the Medical Research Council Unit in Gambia, Dr. Scott Filler from the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria in Geneva, and Dr. Caroline Jones, a senior social scientist at the KEMRI Wellcome Trust Research Programme in Kenya. Other members included Professor Neil Lobo from the University of Notre Dame in the United States and Dr. Melanie Renshaw from the African Leaders Malaria Alliance. The WHO guidelines for malaria, finalized on October 16, 2023, were developed with input from systematic review teams and experts. These teams included individuals such as Ms. Kallista Chan and Ms. Joanna Furnival-Adams from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, Mr. Leslie Choi from the Cochrane Infectious Diseases Group at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, and Professor Paul Garner from the same institution. Additional contributors included Dr. Jo Leonardi-Bee and Dr. Elisa Martello from the University of Nottingham, Dr. Louisa Messenger and Dr. Lucy Paintain from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, and Ms. Laura Paris from The MENTOR Initiative in the United Kingdom. The systematic review team for 2022 and 2023 included Dr. Timothy Hugh Barker, Dr. Jennifer C. Stone, and Ms. Sabira Hasanoff from the JBI Adelaide GRADE Centre at the University of Adelaide in Australia. Other contributors included Ms. Carrie Price from Towson University in Maryland, USA, and Dr. Alinune Kabaghe from the Training and Research Unit of Excellence in Malawi. Professor Zachary Munn from the University of Adelaide served as a guidelines methodologist and co-chair. The WHO required all members of the Guideline Development Group (GDG), ERG, and systematic review teams to declare any interests related to the topics under discussion. These declarations were assessed by the WHO Secretariat with support from the Office of Compliance, Risk Management, and Ethics. For example, Dr. Lucy Tusting declared receiving research funding exceeding £5,000 for studies on the impact of housing improvements on malaria. She was recused from decision-making discussions related to housing modifications to prevent malaria. Similarly, Dr. Umberto d’Alessandro declared receiving research funding for projects on improved housing and malaria prevention, while Dr. Jenifer Armistead reported involvement in projects related to insecticide-treated nets and housing modifications. The ERG members’ expertise was deemed valuable for identifying factual errors, providing clarity, and commenting on implementation considerations, particularly regarding gender, social determinants, equity, and human rights. However, their role did not involve altering the recommendations formulated by the GDG. The WHO guidelines also included recommendations for chemoprevention and malaria vaccines. The GDG for chemoprevention included experts such as Professor Salim Abdulla, who declared involvement in research grants related to malaria chemoprevention, and Professor Miriam Laufer, who declared research grants related to intermittent preventive treatment (IPT) during pregnancy and in schoolchildren. These interests were assessed, and members were allowed to participate in discussions, with some restrictions on voting or chairing sessions. The malaria vaccine recommendations were developed with input from the Malaria Policy Advisory Group (MPAG), the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts (SAGE), and the RTS,S/AS01 MPAG/SAGE Working Group. Members included Dr. Samira Abdelrahman from the University of Gezira in Sudan and Professor Ahmed Adeel from King Saud University in Saudi Arabia. The guidelines were finalized with contributions from systematic review teams and GRADE analysis subgroups.
